stem: Which of the following is closest to the slope of a line of best fit for the data?
stimulus: A coach recorded the average weekly training distance $x$, in kilometers, and the 5-kilometer race time $y$, in minutes, for each of 8 runners. The results are shown in the scatterplot.

figure.caption: Training Distance and 5-Kilometer Race Time
figure.alt: Scatterplot of 8 runners. The x-axis shows average weekly training distance from 0 to 80 kilometers, with gridlines every 10. The y-axis shows 5-kilometer race time from 18 to 28 minutes, with gridlines every 1. The points trend downward from left to right.

explanation: The points fall from left to right, so the slope is negative. That rules out 27. A line of best fit runs through the middle of the points. It passes close to $(10, 26)$ and $(80, 19)$. Use the axis values, not the number of grid squares: the slope is $\frac{19 - 26}{80 - 10} = \frac{-7}{70} = -0.1$. So each additional kilometer of weekly training goes with a race time about 0.1 minute faster.

A.why: You divided the change in distance by the change in time, $\frac{70}{-7}$, so you got kilometers per minute instead of minutes per kilometer. The slope is the change in $y$, race time, per 1-unit change in $x$, training distance.

B.why: You counted grid squares. From $x = 10$ to $x = 80$ the line covers 7 squares across and drops 7 squares, so it looks like a slope of $-1$. But each square across is 10 kilometers and each square up is only 1 minute. With the axis values, the slope is $\frac{-7}{70} = -0.1$.

D.why: 27 is roughly where the line meets the $y$-axis at $x = 0$, so it is the $y$-intercept, not the slope. The line also falls from left to right, so its slope can't be positive.

stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of a line of best fit for the data in this context?
stimulus: An engineer made 8 samples of a polymer, each with a different glass fiber content $x$, as a percentage of the sample's mass. The engineer then measured the tensile strength $y$ of each sample, in megapascals (MPa). The results are shown in the scatterplot.

figure.caption: Glass Fiber Content and Tensile Strength
figure.alt: Scatterplot of 8 polymer samples. The x-axis shows glass fiber content from 0 to 40 percent of mass, with gridlines every 5. The y-axis shows tensile strength from 40 to 130 megapascals, with gridlines every 10. The points trend upward from left to right.

choices: Tensile strength is predicted to increase by 3 MPa for every increase of 1 percentage point in fiber content.
Tensile strength is predicted to increase by 2 MPa for every increase of 1 percentage point in fiber content.
Tensile strength is predicted to increase by 10 MPa for every increase of 1 percentage point in fiber content.
Fiber content is predicted to increase by 2 percentage points for every increase of 1 MPa in tensile strength.
explanation: A line of best fit through the middle of the points passes close to $(0, 40)$ and $(40, 120)$. Its slope is $\frac{120 - 40}{40 - 0} = \frac{80}{40} = 2$. The $y$-variable is tensile strength in MPa and the $x$-variable is fiber content in percent, so the slope means a predicted increase of 2 MPa in tensile strength for every 1-percentage-point increase in fiber content.

A.why: You divided 120 by 40 using the point at $x = 40$, as if the line passed through the origin. The vertical axis starts at 40 MPa, not 0, so the rise from $x = 0$ to $x = 40$ is $120 - 40 = 80$, not 120. That gives a slope of $\frac{80}{40} = 2$.

C.why: You saw the line rise about one gridline (10 MPa) per gridline across and took that as 10 MPa per percentage point. Each gridline across is 5 percentage points, so the rate is $\frac{10}{5} = 2$ MPa per percentage point.

D.why: You found the right number but swapped the variables. The slope is the change in $y$, tensile strength, per 1-unit change in $x$, fiber content, not fiber content per MPa of strength.

stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of the line of best fit in this context?
stimulus: The scatterplot shows data for 9 adults who moved to the same coastal town: x, the number of years each person has lived there, and y, the percent of that person's vowel sounds pronounced in the local way. The line of best fit is $y = 2.5x + 30$.

figure.caption: Years in Town and Local Vowel Use
figure.alt: Scatterplot of 9 points rising steadily from about (2, 34) to about (18, 74).

choices: The percent of local vowel pronunciations is predicted to increase by 2.5 percentage points for every 4 additional years lived in the town.
The percent of local vowel pronunciations is predicted to increase by 10 percentage points for every 4 additional years lived in the town.
The percent of local vowel pronunciations is predicted to increase by 4 percentage points for every 10 additional years lived in the town.
The percent of local vowel pronunciations is predicted to increase by 1.6 percentage points for every 4 additional years lived in the town.
explanation: The slope is 2.5, so y is predicted to go up 2.5 percentage points for each 1 additional year. Every choice talks about 4 years, so scale it up: 4 × 2.5 = 10 percentage points for every 4 years.

A.why: 2.5 is the change for 1 year. You kept it but changed the time span to 4 years without multiplying by 4.

C.why: You swapped which variable is which. This works out to 0.4 percentage point per year, which is the reciprocal of the slope, not the slope.

D.why: You divided 4 by 2.5 when you should have multiplied 2.5 by 4 to get the change over 4 years.

stimulus: The scatterplot shows the weekly running distance and the resting heart rate for 9 recreational runners.

figure.caption: Running Distance and Resting Heart Rate

explanation: The data fall from left to right, so the slope is negative. A line through the data goes from about 68 beats per minute at 10 km to about 52 beats per minute at 90 km. That is a change of −16 over 80 km, so the slope is −16/80 = −0.2.

A.why: You divided the run by the rise (80/−16), which gives kilometers per beat per minute instead of beats per minute per kilometer.

B.why: You counted grid squares. The line drops about one square for each square across, but one square is 2 beats per minute vertically and 10 km horizontally, so the slope is 2/10, not 1.

D.why: You got the size right but missed that the data fall from left to right, so the slope has to be negative.

stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of the line of best fit in this context?
stimulus: In a study of how stories change as they are passed along, a folktale was retold by one person to the next in a chain. The scatterplot shows data for 11 points in the chain: x, the number of retellings the tale had been through, and y, the number of the original plot details still present. The line of best fit can be written as $2y + 3x = 48$.

figure.caption: Plot Details Kept Across Retellings
figure.alt: Scatterplot of 11 points falling from about (1, 23) to about (11, 8).

choices: The number of plot details present is predicted to decrease by 3 for each additional retelling.
The number of plot details present is predicted to decrease by 2 for every 3 additional retellings.
The number of plot details present is predicted to increase by 3 for every 2 additional retellings.
The number of plot details present is predicted to decrease by 3 for every 2 additional retellings.
explanation: Solve for y: 2y = −3x + 48, so y = −1.5x + 24. The slope is −1.5, or −3/2, so the number of details is predicted to drop by 3 for every 2 additional retellings.

A.why: You read the coefficient of x as the slope without first dividing both sides by 2 to get y by itself.

B.why: You solved for x instead of y, which gives the change in retellings per detail (−2/3). Then you described it as if it were the change in details per retelling.

C.why: You got the size right but lost the sign when you moved 3x across the equals sign. The data clearly fall, so the slope is negative.

stimulus: The scatterplot shows the air temperature recorded at the same hour at 10 weather stations on one mountain, along with the elevation of each station.

figure.caption: Elevation and Air Temperature
figure.alt: Scatterplot of 10 points falling from about (2, 23) to about (29, 7).

choices: The temperature is predicted to decrease by 0.6 °C for every 1-meter increase in elevation.
The temperature is predicted to decrease by 1 °C for every 100-meter increase in elevation.
The temperature is predicted to decrease by 5 °C for every 300-meter increase in elevation.
The temperature is predicted to decrease by 0.6 °C for every 100-meter increase in elevation.
explanation: A line through the data goes from about 24 °C at 0 to about 6 °C at 30. That is a drop of 18 °C over 30 units, or 0.6 °C per unit. Each unit on the x-axis is 100 meters, so the temperature drops 0.6 °C for every 100 meters of elevation.

A.why: You found 0.6 correctly but missed that the x-axis is in hundreds of meters, so you treated each unit as 1 meter.

B.why: You counted grid squares. The line drops about one square per square across, but one square is 3 °C vertically and 500 meters horizontally.

C.why: You swapped rise and run: 5 hundred meters over 3 °C. That rate is about 1.7 °C per 100 meters, nearly three times too steep.

stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of a line of best fit for the data?
stimulus: At a monitoring well, hydrologists measure the depth to the water table, which is the distance from the ground surface down to the top of the groundwater. The scatterplot shows this depth, in meters, measured once a year, where x is the number of years since 2010.

figure.caption: Depth to Water Table at One Well
figure.alt: Scatterplot of 11 points rising from about (0, 12) to about (10, 20).

choices: The depth to the water table is predicted to increase by 0.8 meter each year.
The level of the water table is predicted to rise by 0.8 meter each year.
The depth to the water table is predicted to increase by 4 meters each year.
The depth to the water table is predicted to increase by 1.25 meters each year.
explanation: A line through the data goes from about 12 m at year 0 to about 20 m at year 10, so the slope is 8/10 = 0.8 meter per year. The y-variable is depth below the surface, so a positive slope means the depth increases by 0.8 m each year.

B.why: You read the rising graph as a rising water level. A greater depth to the water table means the water level is going down, not up.

C.why: You counted grid squares. The line climbs about 4 squares for each square across, but each square across is 5 years, not 1.

D.why: You divided run by rise (10/8), which gives years per meter. You then described it as meters per year.

stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of the line of best fit in this context?
stimulus: The scatterplot shows data for 9 volunteers in a vaccine trial: x, the dose each received, in micrograms, and y, each volunteer's antibody level four weeks later, in thousands of units per milliliter. The line of best fit is $y = 0.04x + 1.2$.

figure.caption: Vaccine Dose and Antibody Level
figure.y_label: Antibody level (thousands of units per mL)
figure.alt: Scatterplot of 9 points rising from about (5, 1.5) to about (45, 2.9).

choices: The antibody level is predicted to increase by 0.04 unit per milliliter for each additional microgram of dose.
The antibody level is predicted to increase by 1,200 units per milliliter for each additional microgram of dose.
The antibody level is predicted to increase by 40 units per milliliter for each additional microgram of dose.
The antibody level is predicted to increase by 25 units per milliliter for each additional microgram of dose.
explanation: The slope is 0.04, and y is measured in thousands of units per milliliter. So each additional microgram adds 0.04 × 1,000 = 40 units per milliliter.

A.why: You took the slope straight from the equation and missed that y is in thousands of units, so 0.04 means 40 units.

B.why: You used the y-intercept, 1.2 thousand units, which is the predicted level at a dose of 0, not the change per microgram.

D.why: You flipped the slope (1/0.04 = 25), which gives micrograms per thousand units. You then described it as units per microgram.

stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of the line of best fit in this context?
stimulus: The scatterplot shows wing length x, in millimeters, and body mass y, in grams, for 9 adult warblers of one species. Solved for x, the line of best fit is $x = 2y + 40$.

figure.caption: Wing Length and Body Mass of Warblers
figure.alt: Scatterplot of 9 points rising from about (102, 31) to about (134, 46).

choices: Body mass is predicted to increase by 2 grams for each 1-millimeter increase in wing length.
Wing length is predicted to increase by 0.5 millimeter for each 1-gram increase in body mass.
Body mass is predicted to increase by 20 grams for each 1-millimeter increase in wing length.
Body mass is predicted to increase by 0.5 gram for each 1-millimeter increase in wing length.
explanation: Solve for y, the variable on the vertical axis: 2y = x − 40, so y = 0.5x − 20. The slope is 0.5, so body mass is predicted to increase by 0.5 gram for each additional millimeter of wing length.

A.why: You took the coefficient 2 from the equation as given. That equation is solved for x, so 2 is millimeters of wing per gram, not grams per millimeter.

B.why: You kept the right number but swapped the variables. Wing length actually changes by 2 millimeters per gram, so this sentence is false.

C.why: You used the size of the y-intercept, −20, from y = 0.5x − 20 in place of the slope.
